PhD Chemistry

Warda Shahzad

I study how small changes in composition and processing can reshape the structure and optical behavior of semiconductor materials. My doctoral research focuses on Li, Na, and K modified Cu₂ZnSnS₄ (CZTS) thin films, with particular interest in defect engineering, crystallinity, and bandgap control.

01

About

I'm a PhD candidate in Chemistry (Materials Chemistry) at COMSATS University Islamabad (Abbottabad Campus), working on the structural, optical, and electronic properties of kesterite thin films for thin-film solar cells. My research centers on alkali metal doping with lithium, sodium, and potassium, targeting suppression of Cu/Zn antisite defects and secondary phases (ZnS, Cu₂SnS₃), the primary loss mechanisms limiting CZTS device efficiency.

I synthesize films by solution-based chemical deposition and characterize them across XRD, SEM/EDX, and UV-Vis spectroscopy, using Urbach energy and dislocation density as quantitative proxies for defect suppression across each doping series. I'm currently seeking a postdoctoral position to extend this work to new synthesis platforms and semiconductor material systems.

Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Bushra Ismail (bushraismail@cuiatd.edu.pk)
Institution: COMSATS University Islamabad, Abbottabad Campus
02

Research focus

My work is built around a simple question: how can controlled composition and processing be used to improve the structure and optical response of earth abundant semiconductor absorbers?

Li modified CZTS

A processing route for better control

I developed and tested a two step annealing approach for Li modified CZTS. The treatment helped separate the effects of thermal processing from the effect of dopant concentration and was accompanied by improved structural and electrical properties.

Na modified CZTS

Connecting structure with optics

The Na series gave a clear example of how changes in microstrain and optical bandgap can be discussed together, providing a direct structure and optical perspective on the modified CZTS films.

K modified CZTS

Lattice modification and growth

The K series showed lattice expansion together with larger crystallites and a shift in bandgap, while retaining the tetragonal kesterite structure and strong visible light absorption.

Research beyond CZTS

From photocatalysis to photovoltaics

My earlier work on perovskite and graphene oxide composites introduced me to semiconductor bandgap engineering and visible light photocatalysis, which later developed into my current focus on photovoltaic absorber materials.

Make

Solution based chemical deposition followed by controlled thermal treatment.

02

Measure

XRD, SEM, EDS and UV Vis measurements to build a complete picture of each film.

03

Model

Structural and optical analysis including crystallite size, microstrain, bandgap, refractive index and conductivity related parameters.

04

Interpret

Bring the measurements together to explain how processing and composition influence material behavior.

Crystal structure models

VESTA

Optical Materials · 2025 · Li-doped CZTS
Tuned the bandgap from 1.36 to 1.27 eV and reduced dislocation density from 7.3 to 2.13 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² via Li doping and two-step annealing, with electrical conductivity reaching 3.6 Ω⁻¹cm⁻¹.

First-author · PhD research
Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids · 2025 · Na-doped CZTS
Narrowed the bandgap from 1.50 to 1.00 eV and reduced microstrain from 0.37 × 10⁻³ to 0.13 × 10⁻³, establishing a direct structural to optical correlation for Na-induced Cu/Zn antisite suppression in CBD-grown CZTS.

06

Future directions

I would like to build on my experience in defect engineering and solution processed semiconductor materials by working with new absorber systems, synthesis platforms, and defect passivation strategies. I am especially interested in research environments where careful materials synthesis is combined with advanced structural, optical, and electronic characterization.
